learning: If s-bend or slalom still exit with max_error above 0.05 m, the span is not enough and sensor_size or spacing is the next lever. If oval oscillation stays above 0.2 with low max_error, reduce weights before changing geometry.
notes: Integrates the Builder's ±0.04 m span with the unchanged iteration 1 controller so the race isolates the span effect. Expected: fewer s-bend and slalom off-track exits with max_error under about 0.05 m.
rationale: Iteration 1 (the ±0.03 m array) finished 13 of 20 oval runs but only 1 of 20 s-bend and 0 of 20 slalom. Every failure is an off-track exit, with max_error at about 0.062 to 0.063 m and 1.1 to 1.3 line-loss events per run on the sharp tracks. The Builder's geometry change widens the span to ±0.04 m at 0.02 m spacing, keeps y = 0.06 m, sensor_size 0.012 m, wheel_track 0.11 m, mass 0.7 kg and wheel_radius 0.03 m. I supply that geometry as written. Oval steering_oscillation was 0.31 with max_error 0.044, so the oscillation is not coming from error. The Builder asked me to separate span from weight scaling, so I keep the iteration 1 controller (kp 2.5, ki 0, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.2, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], last_direction) unchanged. Any change in results can then be attributed to the wider span. Speed is not limiting (oval finishes in 1.83 s), so wheel_radius stays at 0.03. Expected result: fewer s-bend and slalom off-track exits with max_error below about 0.05 m, and oval finish rate held near 13 of 20. If oscillation stays above 0.2 with low max_error next race, the next step is to scale weights to [-1,-0.5,0,0.5,1], not to change geometry.
